from_quote: The sixth article of the new constitution provides, that the continental laws shall be the supreme law of the land, and that all judges in the separate states shall be bound thereby, anything in the constitution or laws of any state to the contrary notwithstanding
rationale: The paragraph names "the sixth article" and reproduces the wording of its second clause, ending verbatim with "in the constitution or laws of any state to the contrary notwithstanding."
to_quote: shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding

from_quote: All the state officers are also bound by oath to support this constitution
rationale: Continuing its account of the sixth article, the paragraph names the oath binding state officers to support the Constitution, which is Article VI, clause 3.
to_quote: shall be bound by Oath or Affirmation, to support this Constitution

from_quote: Causes of all kinds, between citizens of different states, are to be tried before a continental court
rationale: The paragraph names the federal courts' jurisdiction over causes between citizens of different states, one of the categories listed in Article III, Section 2, clause 1.

from_quote: Authority is also given to the continental courts, to try all causes between a state and its own citizens
rationale: The paragraph names the grant to the federal courts of causes between a state and citizens; controversies between a state and citizens are listed in Article III, Section 2, clause 1, and the next paragraph calls this "the clause relating to causes between the state and individuals."

from_quote: a clause in the new constitution which empowers Congress to keep one at all times
rationale: The paragraph refers to "a clause in the new constitution" empowering Congress to keep a standing army; the army power is Article I, Section 8, clause 12 ("To raise and support Armies").
